AGENDA
  GLENDALE WATER AND POWER COMMISSION
  VIA TELECONFERENCE ONLY
 Welcome to the meeting of the Glendale Water and Power Commission. Meetings are broadcast
 live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for
 program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office.
 Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at
 https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal. If you have any question about
 matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the Glendale Water & Power
 Administration Office at (818) 548-2107 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Glendale Water & Power Administration Office,
 141 N. Glendale Ave., Suite 450, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  MAY 3, 2021 AT 4:00 PM

Due to the evolving situation with the COVID-19 novel coronavirus and health recommendations from
the LA County Health Department, the Glendale Water and Power Commission meeting will be
available to the public electronically.

Due to social distancing requirements, the public will not be able to attend the meeting. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social distancing.

The meeting can be viewed:
On local cable: Charter Cable Channel 6 and AT&T U-verse Channel 99.
Streaming Online: https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal

For public comments and questions during the meeting call (818) 937-8100.

MINUTES
  GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  VIA TELECONFERENCE

  Monday, May 03, 2021, 4:00 PM

Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, social distancing requirements, and health recommendations
from LA County Public Health Department, this meeting was conducted remotely. All GWP Commission
members and staff utilized video conferencing in order to virtually participate in the meeting.

1. ROLL CALL
  The meeting was called to order at 4:00 p.m.

  Present: President Flanigan, Commissioners Jazmadarian, Kedikian, Lall, and Peterson.

2. GWP COMMISSION/ STAFF COMMENTS
  President Flanigan welcomed Mr. John Takhtalian as Interim General Manager for GWP.
  Mr. Takhtalian thanked Messrs. Craig Kuennen, Mark Young, Michael De Ghetto, and Dan
  Scorza for their work serving as Interim General Managers for the past few months.

  Commissioner Lall inquired about in-person meetings, and Mr. Takhtalian responded that
  the Commissioners might meet in person in June if staff and commissioners can be
  accommodated. Therefore, the Commissioners agreed to meet in person for the June 7, 2021
  Commission meeting.

  Commissioner Kedikian suggested former GWP General Manager Steve Zurn be
  acknowledged for his service with GWP; Mr. Takhtalian suggested contacting Mr. Zurn to
  attend in person to receive official recognition for his service, if possible. President Flanigan
  suggested presenting a certificate or plaque to Mr. Zurn at the June 7th meeting.

3. REPORTS – INFORMATION
  a. Urban Water Management Plan
  Mr. Mike De Ghetto, Chief Assistant General Manager - Water, presented the 2021 Urban
  Water Management Plan (UWMP). Mr. De Ghetto acknowledged Water Engineering staff
  members for their efforts on the UWMP: Graciela Zapata, Civil Engineering Associate, Raja
  Takidin, Sr. Civil Engineer, and Richard Ruyle, Water Services Administrator.

  Mr. De Ghetto gave an overview of the procedure for adopting the UWMP and the next
  steps. He stated the UWMP is adopted every five years and submitted to the California
  Department of Water Resources (DWR) to compile a statewide report. The City Council
  will hold a June 8, 2021, public hearing to consider the adoption of the UWMP and the
  Water Shortage Contingency Plan. Mr. Ruyle gave an overview of the UWMP Overview
  and the Water Shortage Contingency Plan, covering Glendale’s water sources, regional
  investments, water usage, demand reduction actions, annual trends in water use, demand
  management measures, and future actions to manage water supply. Mr. De Ghetto and Mr.
  Ruyle responded to questions from Commissioners.
  1
   b. Water Risk Resilience
  Mr. De Ghetto presented an update on GWP's Water Risk Resilience. First, he provided a
  historical background on the events leading to water infrastructure risk management efforts,
  such as September 11, 2001, and the resulting regulations, including the Homeland
  Security Act, America's Water Infrastructure Act of 2018, and cybersecurity laws. Next, Mr.
  De Ghetto discussed the 2018 code updates and regulatory changes that followed the 2017
  Oroville Dam failure. Finally, Mr. De Ghetto discussed new inundation maps updated and
  submitted to the Division Safety of Dams (DSOD). These new emergency response plans
  were submitted to the California Office of Emergency Service (CAL-OES) and commended
  Ms. Zapata's staff for her work on this effort. Finally, he described GWP's internal Water
  Emergency Tactical Plan, updated annually.

  Commissioner Jazmadarian asked about the availability of emergency generators to
  allocate water in case of an earthquake. Mr. De Ghetto responded that our reservoir
  storage could meet the demands for one day of emergency service for fire protection; one
  portable generator can run the biggest pump, and some smaller generators can be used in
  other areas. However, he noted that the purchase of big generators will need the assistance
  of consultants due to electrical work and Air Quality Management District (AQMD) permits
  and will take a year or two to implement. Commissioner Kedikian suggested that the GWP
  Commission provide input before any Council recommendation on funding for the
  generators.

  c. Power System Emergency Response
  Mr. Dan Scorza, Chief Assistant General Manager – Electric, described the Power System
  Emergency Response efforts. He noted that some parts of the emergency plan are
  available for view on the City’s web page, while other sections are confidential. The main
  goal for residents is to restore power as soon as possible.

  Mr. Scorza stated emergency response events include severe weather events,
  earthquakes, fire, and floods. He outlined key points to the emergency response and
  hardening of the GWP Grid, especially during an earthquake and responding to an
  infrastructure failure (“tripping” due to shaking of electrical and mechanical components). He
  stated that the GWP dispatchers/field crews work 24/7/365 and are ready to respond to
  rain, shine, or any other events to restore the GWP Grid within 30 minutes after a major
  earthquake. In addition, the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system
  gives our local Grid Operators (dispatchers) the status of the local grid and the ability to turn
  on and off components to ensure power remotely. Mr. Scorza also noted that GWP
  participates in mutual aid arrangements with other utilities to assist in times of major
  emergencies.

  President Flanigan asked, in the wake of the recent freezing temperatures/outages in
  Texas, could the same situation happen in Glendale in extreme heat or cold events (i.e.,
  local internet service is lost)? Mr. Scorza responded that for heating purposes, one of the
  necessities is learning the weaknesses and installing extra equipment so that no piece of
  equipment becomes overloaded. He stated that GWP is upgrading its system from 4kV to
  12kV to accommodate more solar and more EV charging. Additionally, he noted that GWP
  is interconnected with the adjacent utilities such as Los Angeles, Burbank, and Texas did
  not have that advantage.

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  2
   None.

5. AGENDA FORECAST
  President Flanigan suggested adding a Renewables Portfolio update and Virtual Power Plant
  update for June 7, 2021, Commission Meeting and asked about the status of the Grayson
  Power Project.

  Ms. Christine Godinez, Principal Assistant City Attorney, stated that the Environmental Impact
  Report (EIR) for the Grayson Power Project is still being finalized and suggested July or August
  for a meeting on the topic. The Grayson Power Project item was added to the August meeting
  as a placeholder per President Flanigan. Commissioner Lall concurred with the request for a
  status update on the Grayson Power Project.

  Commissioner Kedikian asked about the budget presentation and whether it will be ready for
  the June 7th Commission meeting. He wondered whether it would be a utility budget
  presentation or a Cost of Service Analysis? Messrs. Scorza and Kuennen responded that the
  budget presentation would be a GWP Operating Budget similar to what will be presented at the
  City Council meeting. John Takhtalian proposed a special presentation of the GWP Budget
  Presentation on June 1, 2021, a virtual meeting.

6. ADJOURNMENT
  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Kedikian
  Seconded by: President Flanigan
  Motion Passed.

The meeting was adjourned at 5:53 p.m.
